name: The Birthday Party
label: 4AD
lede: Five Caulfield Grammar boys took a Melbourne ballroom residency to London, then Berlin, and made noise so ugly and exact that the band couldn't survive it. What walked out of the wreckage was Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds.

eras.title: A school band finds a second guitarist
eras.text: The nucleus formed at Caulfield Grammar in suburban Melbourne and spent years on Lou Reed, Bowie and Alice Cooper covers before punk arrived. As the Boys Next Door they took a residency at the Crystal Ballroom in St Kilda, and in 1978 Rowland S. Howard turned them into something stranger.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party · Wikipedia: Nick Cave
years.h: Cave, Harvey and Calvert start a band at Caulfield Grammar
years.p: [[Nick Cave|4aae17a7-9f0c-487b-b60e-f8eafb410b1d]], [[Mick Harvey|633ec771-1192-4a63-9e19-2ee6a29d1d22]] and Phill Calvert play covers at the Melbourne school; several of them also sing in the school choir. [[Tracy Pew|9f1d70cc-f426-430a-97b1-04b23d006f86]] joins on bass in 1975.
years.xp: The early set leaned on Lou Reed, David Bowie, Roxy Music and Alice Cooper. When the Saints and Radio Birdman broke open Australian punk in 1976, the band started covering Blitzkrieg Bop and Gloria, and by November 1977, as the Boys Next Door, they were playing originals like Sex Crimes.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party
years.h: Rowland S. Howard joins on second guitar
years.p: Howard, from the Young Charlatans, brings feedback, free jazz and rockabilly into the band. Producer Tony Cohen and Missing Link boss Keith Glass come into the picture the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Shivers · Wikipedia: The Birthday Party
yt: Shivers, the Boys Next Door clip
years.h: Cave sings the song Howard wrote at 16
years.p: Shivers, written by Howard in the Young Charlatans, is the only single from Door, Door on Mushroom. It sells out its first pressing and becomes an Australian underground hit.
years.xp:
At the January 1979 session at Richmond Recorders, Cohen suggested Howard sing his own song; Cave insisted on singing it. Howard later said the result was "completely different from what I intended," since he'd written it as an ironic comment on how his friends dramatized romance.

It stayed his most-requested song for decades. The Screaming Jets took a cover to No. 19 in Australia in 1993; Courtney Barnett and Julia Jacklin have covered it too.

eras.title: London, John Peel and a song about bats
eras.text: In 1980 the band renamed itself the Birthday Party and moved to London, where it found the city cold and the audiences slow. John Peel played them anyway, 4AD put the records out in the UK, and the live shows earned them a reputation for violence.

years.cap: The band in a Kilburn pub, London
years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party · Wikipedia: Nick Cave · From the Archives · Louder: Mick Harvey
years.h: The Boys Next Door land in London as the Birthday Party
years.p: The new name comes from Cave and Howard talking about ritual and celebration. Cave's girlfriend, the artist Anita Lane, comes too, and Peel starts booking sessions.
years.xp:
Howard explained the name in 2008: what he and Cave had talked about was "a sense of celebration and making things into more an occasion and ritual." In London the band's shows, with Cave shrieking and throwing himself around, earned them a reputation as the most violent live band in the world.

They left Melbourne on February 29, 1980, and played their first London show as the Birthday Party on June 29 at the Rock Garden in Covent Garden. Harvey later put the plan plainly: 'Our mission was to destroy rock'n'roll from within.'

years.cap: Cave on stage at the Tivoli Hotel, Adelaide, January 1981
q: It stinks, quite honestly ... The engineer slept through the entire session.
years.src: Wikipedia: Prayers on Fire
years.h: Prayers on Fire, with brass from Equal Local
years.p: Cut in Melbourne over December 1980 and January 1981 with Tony Cohen, out on Missing Link and licensed to 4AD. It reaches No. 4 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp: Members of the Melbourne band Equal Local played the horns on Nick the Stripper, and saxophonist Mick Hauser got credited as "Mick Hunter." Pew's review of his own record was not kind.

years.src: Wikipedia: Release the Bats
yt: Release the Bats, live at the Hacienda, 1982
years.h: Release the Bats was meant as a joke
years.p: Harvey's description of the 4AD single, recorded after midnight at Townhouse in London while Phil Collins had the daytime slots. Goth adopted it anyway; it hits No. 3 on the indie chart.
years.xp:
Producer Nick Launay remembered the band walking in looking like they hadn't slept in days. On the B-side, Blast Off, the guitarists pranked Cave into retake after retake until he nearly collapsed; Launay used the first take and then cranked the mid-range on the guitars in revenge.

The song was a send-up of the band's own gothic image, and Cave later dismissed the goth genre it helped start. NME still put it at No. 7 on its list of the greatest goth tracks.

eras.title: The bass player goes to prison, the drummer goes home
eras.text: Junkyard was built to sound like trash, and the year around it nearly took the band apart: Tracy Pew in jail, a rotating bass chair, Calvert out and Harvey moving to drums. By the end of 1982 they'd left London for West Berlin.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tracy Pew · Wikipedia: Junkyard · Wikipedia: The Birthday Party · The Quietus
years.h: Tracy Pew gets ten weeks in HM Prison Won Wron
years.p: Pew is sentenced in Australia for drink driving and theft. Chris Walsh, [[Barry Adamson|a50a1afa-23eb-4ba6-9faf-5dec260898ca]] and Howard's brother Harry Howard take turns on bass until he's back in July.
years.xp:
Walsh covered February, Adamson April and May, Harry Howard June and early July. Adamson plays on Kiss Me Black on Junkyard.

Adamson and Harry Howard each did four or five shows, and some dates were cancelled.

years.src: Wikipedia: Junkyard · From the Archives · The Quietus
years.h: Hot rod artist Ed Roth draws the cover for Junkyard
years.p: Cut in Melbourne and London, with Ed Roth and Dave Christensen on the art. It's No. 1 on the UK indie chart and their second and last studio album.
years.xp:
Cave and Harvey wanted it to "sound like trash. A scratchy, trebly sound." Harvey pushed jungle tom-tom rhythms and played drums on several tracks himself. Anita Lane co-wrote Dead Joe and Kiss Me Black.

The writer Julian Marszalek said it still sounds like it's waiting for rock music to catch up with it. It ranked No. 17 in the book 100 Best Australian Albums.

Sessions started in mid-December 1981 at Armstrong Audio Video in South Melbourne, with Tony Cohen engineering most of it and piling on treble. 'We were pushing that deliberately beyond what was acceptable,' Harvey told the Quietus.

years.cap: Cave at The Ace, Brixton, November 1982
years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party · Wikipedia: Phill Calvert · Wikipedia: Mick Harvey
years.h: Calvert is out and Harvey takes over the drums
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Calvert couldn't nail the beat of Dead Joe to everyone's satisfaction. He goes on to tour America with [[The Psychedelic Furs|9f930ddf-be2f-4de5-a39f-7ae47305752e]].

years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party
years.h: Cave and Harvey take their names off Honeymoon in Red
years.p: The album with [[Lydia Lunch|74f2add6-e8b6-4323-a21b-443600379d16]] gets overdubbed and mixed in ways Cave and Harvey hate. Howard and Pew keep their credits; it doesn't come out until 1987.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party · Wikipedia: Mick Harvey · The Quietus
years.h: Done with London, the band moves to West Berlin
years.p: After a run of London shows in August, the four of them relocate. The Berlin period is louder and more aggressive, and brings them into the orbit of [[Einstürzende Neubauten|6e9ac29b-798c-4af7-8d9e-55cdc72a999c]].

eras.title: Berlin, then the Crystal Ballroom one last time
eras.text: The Berlin records are the band at its most exact and most frightening. They are also the sound of Cave and Howard pulling apart, and by June the Birthday Party was finished, playing its last show in the same St Kilda room where the Boys Next Door had built a following.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party · Wikipedia: Mutiny · Louder: Mick Harvey
yt: Live at First Avenue, Minneapolis, April 1983
years.h: The Bad Seed EP comes out on 4AD
years.p: Four songs with Harvey on drums. Its title will turn into the name of Cave's next band.
years.xp: Recorded in October 1982 at Hansa Studios in Berlin. Harvey's writing share had been climbing: one co-write on Prayers on Fire, three on Junkyard, and by this EP, he said, 'I was basically co-writing all the music.'

years.cap: Flyer for the Birthday Party with Einsturzende Neubauten at the Lyceum, London, 7 March 1983
years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party
years.h: Blixa Bargeld plays guitar on Mutiny in Heaven
years.p: The [[Einstürzende Neubauten|6e9ac29b-798c-4af7-8d9e-55cdc72a999c]] leader sits in on the session. Harvey leaves soon after, as the split between Cave and Howard widens.

years.cap: Pew and Cave at the last show, St Kilda, 9 June 1983
years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party
years.h: The last show is back at the Crystal Ballroom
years.p: With Des Hefner on drums for the final tour, the band ends where it started, in St Kilda. The split between Cave and Howard, and the toll of work and drugs, end it.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party · Rate Your Music · Wikipedia: Mutiny · Louder: Mick Harvey
years.h: Mutiny! arrives after the band is gone
years.p: The final EP comes out on Mute and closes with Mutiny in Heaven. Cave, Harvey and Adamson are already forming [[Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds|172e1f1a-504d-4488-b053-6344ba63e6d0]]; Howard goes on to Crime and the City Solution and [[These Immortal Souls|502f5022-ed77-48d9-b92c-b6c73fa9715a]].
years.xp: Sessions started at Hansa in April 1983 and finished in London in August, after the Australian tour. Harvey: 'it was pretty hard squeezing those songs out... It had lost its immediacy and energy.'

eras.title: Two founders gone, one night back together
eras.text: Pew died young and Howard didn't make it to 51. In between, the Birthday Party played one more time, unannounced, inside a Bad Seeds set in London.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tracy Pew
years.h: Tracy Pew dies in Melbourne at 28
years.p: Pew dies of a brain hemorrhage from head injuries suffered during an epileptic seizure in his bath. He had been studying literature and philosophy at Monash University and played on the Bad Seeds' Kicking Against the Pricks.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party
years.h: Howard joins the Bad Seeds and the old songs come back
years.p: At an NME charity show in London, Howard walks on with Cave and Harvey for Wild World, Dead Joe and Nick the Stripper.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Birthday Party
years.h: Cave brings Howard and Pew into the ARIA Hall of Fame
years.p: Inducted himself, Cave uses his speech to induct the Australian Bad Seeds, Harvey among them, plus Howard and Pew.

years.cap: Rowland S. Howard on stage, January 2009
q: Australia's most unique, gifted and uncompromising guitarist.
years.src: Wikipedia: Rowland S. Howard
years.h: Rowland S. Howard dies at 50, months after Pop Crimes
years.p: Howard dies of liver cancer, with his second solo album just out to strong reviews. St Kilda names a laneway after him in 2013.

years.src: Guardian: Mutiny in Heaven · Louder Than War: Mutiny in Heaven
years.h: Mutiny in Heaven puts the band on screen
years.p: Ian White's 98-minute documentary runs from Melbourne to the end, with animation by the German comics artist Reinhard Kleist filling in for scenes nobody filmed.
years.xp: It opens on a young Cave on stage, cigarette in hand, warning: 'The front row is not for the fragile.' Harvey sums up the band's approach an hour in: 'We didn't do anything to try and be likable.'
